purpose: Group-aware, leakage-checked development-era split of the schema-v2 weak-labelled source pool. This programme is independent of and does not wait for T14B/T14C manual adjudication.
seed_notes: Fixed integer seed used for all deterministic pseudo-random group ordering. Changing this seed changes split membership and must bump policy_version.

protected_status.note: source_holdout is a development-era holdout used for early model-selection and threshold checks. It is NOT the final protected manual benchmark (manual_protected_challenge_set) defined in cursor_plan/08_manual_gold_dataset_program.md and cursor_plan/tickets/T15_gold_splits_leakage_and_eligibility.md. The manual_protected_challenge_set remains gated on T14C adjudication and is out of scope for this programme.

auxiliary_weak_pool.note: ClariQ is auxiliary only. It is never eligible for robot-facing metrics (route, risk, capability, rejection) and is split separately into auxiliary_train / auxiliary_dev only (no auxiliary_holdout).

excluded_sources.name: TEACh
excluded_sources.reason: Not part of the approved canonical weak-pool converters (T03-T09); excluded from this split programme entirely.

excluded_sources.name: t13_calibration
excluded_sources.reason: T13 calibration (n=24) is annotation-process calibration only; forbidden as development gold, bake-off, training, or synthetic evaluator input.

excluded_sources.name: future_manual_namespace
excluded_sources.reason: The future manual_protected_challenge_set (~300 adjudicated records) does not exist yet and must never influence source development splits, model selection, training, or thresholds.

excluded_sources.name: model_selection_development_set_v1
excluded_sources.reason: Frozen 40-record development bake-off set (T12/T16-T24 pipeline transport). Must stay disjoint from source splits by id and by normalised command text.

excluded_sources.name: synthetic_evaluator_fixtures
excluded_sources.reason: Hand-authored interface/evaluator fixtures used for pipeline smoke testing are not source data and must not leak into or from the splits.

tolerance.description: Maximum allowed absolute deviation between the realised split percentage and the target ratio, measured per split over the whole primary pool and separately over the whole auxiliary pool.

grouping_rules.description: Deterministic, record-field-derived grouping keys so that no two records from the same lineage/scenario/dialogue/context/candidate family are ever split across source_train / source_dev / source_holdout (or across auxiliary_train / auxiliary_dev).

precedence.detail: If the schema-v2 record's `group_id` field is non-null, the group key is `group:<group_id>`. Covers AmbiK plan-group siblings, CoDraw-iCR v2 game/dialogue families, CLARA scene families, and ClariQ topic families.

If `group_id` is null but the record `id` ends in an `@<turn>` suffix or a `__frame_<n>` suffix, the group key is `lineage:<source_dataset>:<id-without-suffix>`. Covers VAGUE multi-turn / multi-frame context variants from the same source video.

Otherwise, the group key is `cmd:<source_dataset>:<sha256(normalised command)[:16]>`. Keeps exact-duplicate and near-duplicate-by-normalisation commands (paraphrase/template repeats) inside a single dataset together in one split.

grouping_rules.candidate_pair_variants: Candidate interpretation frames are stored nested inside a single canonical record (candidate_interpretations[]), so they never require separate grouping; they always stay together because they belong to one record.
grouping_rules.same_lineage_or_seed: Records sharing a group key from any of the three rules above are always assigned to exactly one split as a unit; the split assignment never inspects individual member content.

stratification_notes: Stratification operates at group granularity using the group's lowest-id member as the representative record. Coarse axes are used deliberately (dataset x ambiguity bucket) to keep every stratum large enough for a stable 70/15/15 (or 85/15) split under group-aware constraints.

assignment_algorithm.name: seeded_digest_order_greedy_proportional
steps: 1. Compute a group key for every record using grouping_rules.
2. Compute a stratum key per group from its representative record.
3. Within each stratum, order groups deterministically by sha256(f'{seed}:{group_key}') so ordering only depends on the fixed seed and the group key content, never on dict/set iteration order.

4. Walk the ordered groups once; for each group, assign it to whichever split currently has the largest deficit between its running record share and its target ratio for that stratum, then update running counts.
5. Aggregate per-stratum assignments; report realised percentages and compare against target_ratios within tolerance.

value_semantics.eligible: Task-relevant field(s) are present with a concrete, usable value for this record.
value_semantics.weakly_eligible: The dataset/record supports this task in principle (per weak-pool label_eligibility policy) but only a partial or low-confidence signal is present.
value_semantics.ineligible: This task structurally does not apply to this record given its source dataset / weak-pool label_eligibility policy (a dataset-design fact, not a missing value).
value_semantics.unavailable: This task could apply in principle but the concrete label/value was not collected for this record. Never treated as a negative label.

eligibility_manifest.invariant: Missing or unknown labels are recorded as 'unavailable' (or 'ineligible' when structurally inapplicable). They are never rewritten as a negative class value for training or evaluation.
